title: We Need a Phone Animal — AI Sales — $35 Per Booked Call — LA Company
description:
Read this carefully before applying.

We are not looking for a cold caller. We are not looking for someone who needs training wheels. We are looking for one person who is genuinely dangerous on the phone — someone who can call a complete stranger, build instant rapport, find the pain, and book a meeting before they even know what hit them.

If that is you — keep reading.

If you are not sure — this is not for you.



Who we are:

Inqora is an AI company based in Los Angeles. We help local businesses — med spas, HVAC companies, law firms — stop losing money from missed calls and slow follow up. Our system responds to every lead in under 10 seconds automatically. Business owners see it and immediately understand what they have been leaving on the table.

The product is real. The results are real. We just need someone who can get the right people on the phone and make them curious enough to take a 15 minute meeting.



What you will do:

Call business owners in Los Angeles from our list. Your only job is to start a real conversation, find out if they have a problem we solve, and book a 15 minute call with our specialist. You are not closing deals. You are opening doors.

One good opener. One good question. One booking. Repeat 80 times a day.



What you earn:

$4 per hour base plus $35 for every booked call that actually shows up.

Here is what that looks like in real numbers:

Book 2 calls a day — $70 in commission plus your base — every single day

Book 3 calls a day — $105 in commission plus your base — every single day

Book 5 calls a day — $175 in commission plus your base — every single day

The best setters we have seen book 3 to 5 calls a day consistently. At $35 per booking that is $2,100 to $3,500 a month in commission alone — on top of your hourly base. Working remotely from wherever you are.

We pay every other Friday. No delays. No excuses.



The only thing we care about:

One specific thing — someone who sounds like a human being on the phone not a robot reading words off a page.

Everything else we handle. We have the list. We have the system. We have the product. We have a specialist who closes the deals once you book the meeting.

We just need someone with the natural ability to make a stranger feel comfortable in 10 seconds and curious in 30.

If you have that — the rest is details.



You are the right person if:

You are a natural on the phone — conversations come easily to you

You handle rejection without flinching — a hang up means nothing to you

You are curious and ask questions instead of just pitching

You are hungry — you want to earn based on what you produce not what you are guaranteed

You are available during US Pacific business hours

You show up every single day without being chased



You are NOT the right person if:

You need a word for word script to function on a call

You get discouraged when people hang up

You have never sold anything over the phone

You ghost employers without notice

You are looking for a comfortable easy job



To apply:

One voice note. 45 seconds maximum.

You just called a business owner cold. They pick up and immediately say I am not interested. What do you say next and how do you say it.

Do not tell us what you would say. Say it. Right now. Into the voice note. As if they are on the other end of the phone.

That voice note is your entire application. If it is good you will hear from us the same day.

description:
Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company

Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. 



This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



What You Get If You Win Here

- High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos

- Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company.

- Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics.

- Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. 

- Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves!

If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: 

Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs.



We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who:

Can’t drive tasks to completion independently

Mark tasks complete with no proof

Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. 

Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru

Need hand-holding 

I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. 



What You’ll Actually Do

You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs:

Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed

Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin)

Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items

Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes

If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.”

title: Customer Service Representative
description:
JOB TITLE:

Customer Service Representative — Remote





JOB DESCRIPTION:



Full-Time · 7:30am–3:30pm MST · $5–$8/hr USD base + performance bonuses




 · Phoenix, Arizona Area · Est. 2021



About Crappy Cleanup



Crappy Cleanup is a fast-growing dog waste removal company serving the Phoenix, Arizona area. We provide recurring and one-time yard cleaning services to hundreds of residential customers across the valley. Our recurring plans range from monthly to three times per week depending on the customer — making us one of the most flexible pet waste removal services in the market. We are a real company with real systems, real culture, and a real growth path for the right people.



We are hiring our first remote Customer Service Representative to help us scale. This is not a task-and-forget VA role. We are looking for someone who wants to grow with us, take ownership of the customer experience, and eventually move into a senior office role as the team expands.



The Role



You will be the voice of Crappy Cleanup to every customer. You handle inbound customer communication, manage our sales pipeline, process cancellation save attempts, pitch service upgrades, and keep our CRM organized and up to date. You follow proven scripts and systems — and you bring your own warmth and professionalism to every interaction.



This is a high trust, high ownership role. We will train you on everything Crappy Cleanup specific. What we cannot train is the communication skill, the customer service instinct, and the drive to do excellent work. You need to bring those.



What You Will Do



- Respond to all inbound customer texts,
s, and messages within 10 minutes during business hours

- Manage our sales pipeline — follow up with new leads, pitch service options, and onboard new customers using GHL

- Handle cancellation save attempts using our proven save script via text and phone

- Actively pitch service upgrades and add-on services to new and existing customers

- Process daily billing — charge new services at start of shift and follow up on failed payments

- Monitor the operations board every morning for missed jobs and scheduling discrepancies

- Log detailed notes after every customer interaction across all platforms

- Send proactive customer follow up messages at key touchpoints after signup

- Process customer account change requests — frequency changes, holds, and updates

- Monitor and re-engage dormant customer accounts

- Support referral program management



Schedule and Hours



This is a full-time remote position working Arizona business hours. Arizona does not observe daylight saving time so our hours are consistent year round.



Hours: Monday through Saturday, 7:30am to 3:30pm Arizona time (MST/UTC-7)

Time Zone: Must be able to work Arizona business hours — MST year round

Days: Monday through Saturday

Location: Fully remote — work from home



Activity Monitoring



This role uses activity monitoring software during work hours to track active time and computer activity. This is standard practice for our remote team and ensures fairness across the board — everyone on the remote team is held to the same standard. If you do excellent work you will have nothing to worry about.



Compensation



Base Pay: $5.00–$8.00 USD per hour depending on experience

Performance Bonuses: Earn bonuses based on service upgrades sold, add-on services enrolled, and customer retention rate. Top performers earn an additional $150 to $300 per month on top of base pay.

Payment: Paid weekly via your preferred method

Growth: Strong performers have a clear path to Office Manager as the team grows



What We Are Looking For



Required:

- Excellent written and spoken English — clear, warm, and professional in every interaction

- Customer service experience — minimum 1 to 2 years in a customer facing role

- Available to work Arizona business hours consistently — no exceptions

- Strong computer skills — comfortable learning new software quickly

- Reliable internet connection and a quiet work environment

- Ability to follow scripts and systems precisely while still sounding human and genuine

- Detail oriented — nothing falls through the cracks on your watch

- Self-motivated — you do not need to be micromanaged to do great work



Preferred — Not Required:

- Experience in a US-based home service, subscription, or service industry company

- Experience with CRM tools — any platform

- Experience with sales, customer retention, or outbound follow up

- Prior experience working with US clients during US business hours

- Typing speed of 50 WPM or higher



Why Crappy Cleanup



- Real systems and real training — comprehensive paid training program with scripts, tools, and processes fully documented before your first day

- Performance bonuses that actually pay out — we built the bonus structure to reward people who perform, not just show up

- A growing company — we are expanding every week and we promote from within

- Direct access to leadership — you will work closely with the Office Manager and co-founders, not lost in a large corporate structure

- Long term opportunity — this role is designed to grow into an Office Manager position for the right person



How to Apply



To be considered for this role you must answer both of the following questions in your application. Applications without answers to both questions will not be reviewed.



Question 1 — Customer Service Scenario

A customer sends you this text: "Hey I want to cancel my service, it's just too expensive right now." Write your response exactly as you would send it to the customer.



Question 2 — Availability

What is your current time zone and what hours are you available to work? Are you able to consistently work Arizona business hours (7:30am to 3:30pm MST)?



We review every application personally. If your application stands out we will reach out within 3 to 5 business days to schedule a video interview.



We are looking for someone who is in this for the long term — not a short term gig. If that sounds like you we would love to hear from you.

title: Video Editor for Commercial Glass And Door Company
description:
Full-Time Video Editor for Commercial Glass & Door Company



 About Our Company



We are a commercial glass, door service, and emergency board-up company based in Southern California. We help businesses keep their storefronts, doors, and glass safe, secure, functional, and professional-looking.



We are building a library of training videos, client education videos, YouTube videos, and short social media videos. We want our content to be useful, clear, professional, and fun to watch.







We value honesty, open communication, good work, and respect for people’s time.



We want someone who will tell us the truth, ask questions when something is unclear, and communicate early if there is a problem with a deadline or assignment.



We do not expect perfection, especially while someone is learning. We do expect reliability, effort, attention to detail, and a willingness to receive feedback and improve.



We believe good systems make work easier for everyone, and we want to work with someone who takes pride in helping us create useful, organized, high-quality videos.



 



We are looking for a full-time Video Editor to help us turn raw video footage into polished, useful, and engaging videos.



You will be watching longer raw videos and pulling out the best parts to create:



* Long-form training videos

* Step-by-step internal training videos

* Customer-facing educational videos

* YouTube videos

* YouTube Shorts

* TikTok videos

* Instagram Reels

* Short promotional or informational videos



This is a full-time role. The workload may vary from week to week, but we do not expect more than 40 hours per week.



 



This position offers flexible hours. You may work during the hours that are best for you and your family, as long as you meet deadlines, communicate clearly, and send a daily report of what was completed.



We are located in California. At first, we will likely have short daily tea
etings. Later, we expect to reduce this to a weekly tea
eting. Our preferred meeting time is around 5:00 PM California time, which is usually around 8:00–9:00 AM Philippine Time depending on daylight savings.



We respect our employees’ free time. We do not expect you to work in the middle of the night. We want someone who can work normal Philippine daytime hours and manage their work responsibly.







We are looking for someone who can work independently, manage their own tasks, meet deadlines, and ask questions when something is unclear.



It is okay not to know everything right away. It is not okay to disappear, guess, or stay silent when you need clarification. We want someone who communicates clearly and is open to feedback.



This should be your primary full-time position. Please do not apply if you are trying to work multiple full-time jobs at the same time.



 



Your responsibilities may include:



* Reviewing raw video footage and identifying the best usable clips

* Editing long training videos from raw footage

* Creating short social media clips from longer videos

* Creating customer-facing educational videos

* Creating engaging hooks and intros

* Adding captions, B-roll, motion text, graphics, music, and transitions

* Cleaning up dead space and keeping the pace strong

* Editing talking-head, tutorial, and voice-driven content

* Creating vertical videos for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, and Instagram Reels

* Organizing finished videos into a clear training and marketing video library

* Creating tables of contents, chapter titles, or section notes for longer videos

* Identifying clips from longer videos that can be reused as short-form social media content

* Organizing video files in Google Drive

* Managing assigned tasks in ClickUp

* Following video templates and helping improve our editing style over time

* Sending a daily update about what you completed, what is still in progress, and where you need help







We want you to take raw video and turn it into usable, engaging, and concise training videos.



We need more than just editing. We also need your help capturing what was taught in the video.



For training videos, you may need to provide:



* A short outline of what was explained

* Step-by-step process notes

* Key points covered in the video

* Any unclear parts that need review

* A clean final video that makes the training easier to understand



You may use AI tools to help create outlines or summaries, but you must understand the English content well enough to check whether the outline is accurate. We need someone with strong English comprehension who can understand the video content, not just run it through AI or translation software.

 Video Library and Table of Contents Responsibilities



We are also building a video library for both employee training and customer education.



You may help organize edited videos into a clear video library so our team can find and use them later.



This may include:



* Organizing training videos by topic, service type, or process

* Organizing customer-facing videos by topic, service, marketing purpose, and target client type, such as facility managers, business owners, property managers, and property owners, so we can better target our marketing

* Creating chapter titles or section labels

* Noting where important steps, examples, or explanations appear in the video

* Identifying which clips should become short videos, training clips, or customer-facing marketing videos

* Keeping video file names, folders, and descriptions organized

* Helping us build a searchable library of training and marketing videos



For technical training videos, we need someone who can understand the content well enough to create a useful outline. For customer-facing videos, we need someone who can understand the message well enough to help us turn the video into clear, helpful, and interesting content.







The ideal candidate should have:



* Strong video editing skills

* Excellent English comprehension

* Ability to understand spoken English in videos

* Experience editing long-form and short-form content

* Experience editing vertical video for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts

* Good sense of pacing, visual storytelling, and snappy intros

* Ability to create engaging hooks

* Comfort working with talking-head videos, tutorials, and voice-driven content

* Ability to add captions, B-roll, motion text, music, and transitions

* Ability to identify the strongest 
nts in raw footage and d
 what should become a training video, customer education video, or short social media clip

* Good organization skills

* Reliable computer and strong internet connection

* Ability to meet deadlines

* Ability to work without close supervision

* Willingness to ask for clarity when needed

* Openness to feedback and revisions



Helpful Experience







* Experience editing for YouTube

* Experience editing for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts



Bonus skills, preferred but can be learned on the job:



* Experience working with shared video files through Google Drive, Dropbox, 
, or similar tools

* Experience using Loom or similar tools for video communication

* Experience with ClickUp or similar task management software

* Experience organizing files in Google Drive

* Experience editing educational or training content

* Experience with construction, local business, trades, home service, glass, doors, or commercial service companies







We are open to the video editing software you prefer, as long as you can create high-quality work, meet deadlines, and deliver finished videos in the formats we need.



Please tell us:



* The top two or three editing programs you prefer to use

* Why you prefer those programs

* What types of videos you usually create with each program

* Whether your portfolio samples were created using those tools

* How you prefer to receive raw video files

* How you prefer to send finished video files for review



Please let us know about your desired pay for this full-time salaried posion: 

* How much do you expect to be paid to start while you learn about our business and figure out the job?

* How much do you expect to be paid once you are able to work completely independently with little supervision?



We currently use or plan to use:



* ClickUp for task management

* Loom for video communication

* Google Drive for file sharing and video storage



We may add other tools later, but we are most interested in your editing skill, judgment, organization, and ability to produce strong finished videos.

To show that you read this carefully, please include "Glass Video Wizard" in the subject line when you apply.





To be considered, you must send links to video samples or a portfolio.



We would especially like to see samples of:



* Long-form YouTube videos

* Short-form vertical videos

* TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts

* Training videos

* Educational videos

* Business or client-facing videos

* Videos created for other companies



Please do not apply without samples. We must be able to review your previous work.







After reviewing applicants, we will choose a small group of finalists.



Finalists may be asked to complete a paid sample project. We will send a raw video sample and ask you to create:



* One usable training video

* One short social media video



This sample project will be paid upon completion, whether or not you are hired.



Only selected finalists will be asked to complete the paid sample project.





This is a full-time salary position.



Pay will depend on experience, skill level, and fit for the role. Pay may start lower during the beginning/training period while we build the workflow, with the opportunity for an increase once we are confident the person is a strong long-term fit.



Payments will be made weekly in U.S. dollars via EasyPay/Payoneer for the first 4–6 months. After the role is established, we will likely move to a biweekly pay schedule.



We offer paid holidays after the role is established.



< Who>



We are looking for someone who is creative, organized, reliable, and self-managed.



The right person will be able to watch raw footage, understand the message, find the useful parts, and turn it into videos that educate and entertain.



You should enjoy making videos clearer, more engaging, and easier to understand.







Please apply through OnlineJobs.ph and include:



* A short message about why you are a good fit for this role

* Links to your portfolio or editing samples

* The top two or three editing software programs you prefer to use

* How you prefer to receive raw video files

* How you prefer to send finished video files for review

* Your expected monthly salary

* Your availability and preferred work schedule in Philippine Time

* Confirmation that you have a reliable computer and a strong internet connection



We are excited to find someone who can help us create useful, fun, and engaging videos that help train our team and educate our clients.

description:
Remote I Part-Time (room for growth) I Growth-Focused Role



We're looking for an experienced B2B Content Writer to join our marketing team who excels at turning research, interviews, and industry insights into original, authoritative blog content that educates HR and benefits leaders, strengthens brand awareness, and drives qualified leads to our service pages.



**This is a long-term opportunity. We're looking for someone who wants to become an extension of our marketing team and grow with us over time.



What we're looking for in our next content writer: 

• 3+ years of experience writing B2B marketing content. 

• Exceptional written English and attention to detail.

• Experience writing for executive audiences.

• A strong understanding of SEO fundamentals (experience with AEO is a plus). 

• The ability to translate complex ideas into engaging content.

• Experience using tools like, Ahrefs, SEMrush, GA4, or similar. 

• Bonus points for experience writing in AP Style.



What we’re not looking for: 

Content writers that embrace credible research, original insights, and thoughtful analysis. If your process is simply prompting AI and making light edits, this role probably isn't the right fit.



What you'll be doing:

• Update and optimize existing blog posts each month to improve SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), readability, and lead generation performance.

• Conduct keyword research and apply on-page SEO best practices, including optimizing titles, headings, meta descriptions, internal links, image alt text, and calls to action.

• Format content for featured snippets, AI Overviews, and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) by writing clear headings, FAQs, concise answers, and scannable content.

• Source high-quality, educational stock photography that enhances the reader experience and supports each article.

• You should be comfortable using AI tools to enhance your workflow while recognizing their limitations. We value writers who use AI to work smarter, not to replace original research, strategic thinking, and high-quality writing.



About Us

We’re a leading employee concierge company in the United States, helping organizations give employees more time for what matters most by handling the everyday tasks that compete for their time and attention. We're proud to be the only U.S. concierge company to earn Great Place to Work® Certification — a recognition that reflects the culture we've built and the people who make it possible.





How to Apply

1. Submit your resume.

2. Submit a link to your portfolio or examples of your work (Preference — B2B content for professional audiences).

title: NetSuite Reporting Consultant
description:
NetSuite Reporting Consultant



We are seeking a qualified NetSuite Reporting Consultant.



About The Company

The Company is a mobile automotive diagnostics and calibration company that partners with collision repair and automotive service centers to deliver specialized technical services, helping ensure vehicles are repaired safely, efficiently, and in accordance with manufacturer standards. This role will report to the Chief Financial Officer.



Position Overview

We are looking for a NetSuite Report Builder to join our team as a functional consultant supporting financial and operational reporting needs within NetSuite. This role is focused on designing, building, and maintaining saved searches, reports, and dashboards that give our team clear visibility into their financial and operational data. 



You will work closely with accounting and business teams to translate reporting requests into accurate, well-structured NetSuite deliverables. While a strong understanding of accounting concepts is essential to interpret and structure financial data correctly, this is not an accounting role.  The focus is on the functional and technical build within NetSuite.



Key Responsibilities

Build and maintain saved searches, reports, and dashboards in NetSuite covering financial reports, budget data, and operational data such as service jobs, technician activity, and shop/manager accounts.

Translate reporting requests from leadership into clear, functional NetSuite deliverables.

Ensure that all reports follow a proper protocol from the request and approval stage, through validation and publication.

Design KPIs and scorecards for job volume, technician utilization, and job-level profitability across service locations.

Partner with the finance team to ensure reports reflect correct account structures and job-costing logic.

Troubleshoot and refine existing reports to improve accuracy and usability.

Document report logic and maintain a library of reusable templates.



Qualifications



Required

Bachelor’s Degree in business or finance, or related field.

Proven experience building reports, saved searches, and dashboards in NetSuite.

Strong business and accounting acumen. Comfortable with financial statements, account structures, and job/project-based cost data.

Experience working in a functional consultant capacity, translating business needs into system solutions.

Strong written and spoken English communication skills, and ability to work independently and demonstrates a high level of self-accountability.





Preferred

NetSuite certification (e.g., SuiteFoundation or ERP Consultant)

Familiarity with SuiteAnalytics Workbooks

Experience with field service, mobile service, or multi-location/job-based businesses





Work Environment

Full-time, remote, independent contractor status

Align to the organization’s Central time zone hours (8 AM - 5 PM CST) 8 hours per day, Monday through Friday.

Candidate must agree to hold this role exclusively, with no other projects or clients, and that no sub-contracting of work will occur.

Candidate must provide a backup device in case of a laptop or equipment failure.

Occasional reporting into a co-work physical office location in Cebu City or Metro Manila for team building and training events.

Competitive independent contractor pay commensurate with experience

US Holiday pay

.

title: Executive Assistant/Operations (Fast Growing)
description:
Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company

Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. 



This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal.



What You Get If You Win Here

- High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos

- Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company.

- Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics.

- Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. 

- Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves!

If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: 

Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace.

Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs.



We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who:

Can’t drive tasks to completion independently

Mark tasks complete with no proof

Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. 

Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru

Need hand-holding 

I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. 



What You’ll Actually Do

You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs:

Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed

Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin)

Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items

Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes

Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects

Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked

We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. 



How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days)

We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want.



Real Growth Example 

One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly.



Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises)

This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment.



What Winning Looks Like

By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you



By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. 



If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.”



Who This Is NOT For

You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence.

You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. 

You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5

You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers

You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps

You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/

You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure

You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side.

You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first.





Who This IS For

You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes

You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall

You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them

You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks

You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs.

You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create.

You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here.  



Comp & Growth

(All of this is written into your contract.)

Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial

• $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit.

• No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors.

Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside

• Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward.

• On top of base, you can earn:

$400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them).

$1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard.

• In practice, that means:

Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month

Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month

All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture.



Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay)

We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat.

We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando
etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls.



Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 

95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. 



Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.



How To Apply (24-Hour Test)

Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises)



If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are:

A short interview focused on your past execution.

A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit.



Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must:



Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine):

Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro
ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” 

Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each.

Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders.

Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list):

– “Fix Asana, it’s a mess”

– “Seller lead texting follow up??”

– “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ”

– “Inventory backlog insane”

– “Need better reporting”

– “Update SOPs

In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager.

In a Google Doc, please:



Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” 

Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points.



Link the Google Doc here (view access).



Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying.



Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.

title: Operations Support Specialist - Logistics
description:
We are a large moving and junk removal company based on Long Island, NY, USA. We have built a customer service, sales & marketing company that happens to do junk removal and moving - we've been featured 5 times on the INC 5000 list of Fastest Growing Companies in America and honored as one of NewsDay's Top Workplaces. We have worked with remote teams all over the world since 2009 and understand how to build long-term working relationships.



We are seeking a sharp, dependable Logistics/Operations Support Specialist who work alongside our local operations team  — tracking crews, catching problems before they become fires, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks on our busiest days.



Responsibilities:

*Keep our internal job management system updated in real time — every job status, crew assignment, arrival, and change reflected accurately as the day unfolds

*Monitor our fleet through Samsara — catch driver issues (speeding, harsh driving, idling, off-route, missed clock-ins) and escalate to the local team immediately

*Schedule and route crews for the day's jobs, then adjust on the fly as cancellations, add-ons, and delays hit

*Push real-time job updates to our local management team and crews throughout the day

*Build and deliver daily and weekly reports on operations, crew performance, and job metrics

*Be our eyes on the operation during weekend peak demand — when volume is highest and there's no room for things to slip





We will teach you all of our internal procedures, but here's what we need from you to succeed in this position:



*Dispatch & Operations experience

...preferred - previous dispatch, logistics coordination, or real-time operations support (transportation, moving, delivery, or trucking a big plus)

...comfortable making quick decisions and adjusting plans in real time

...calm under pressure — you don't rattle when three things go sideways at once during peak



*Technical / Systems skills

...ability to learn new software fast (we'll train you on Samsara and our internal scheduling tools)

...prior experience with dispatch, routing, scheduling, or fleet/GPS platforms

...comfortable working across multiple systems and browser tabs at once

...basic reporting — pulling data and turning it into a clean, useful report



*Communication skills

...strong written and spoken English

...clear, fast, professional communication with drivers, crews, and U.S. management

...proactive — you flag problems before they become fires, you don't wait to be asked



*Reliability

...rock-solid attendance and punctuality — this is a real-time role, your shift can't start late

...a reliable home setup: fast internet, backup mobile data, and a quiet workspace

...self-directed — you own your shift and keep things moving without hand-holding

...available for work hours and weekend coverage as noted below



Schedule:

This position is designed to work 7:00am to 3:00pm EST Wednesday through Sunday.



You will work directly alongside our operations managers on a daily basis (based in New York) and report to our COO.  We also have other remote, PH-based tea
mbers as coworkers in various roles.



This will be your full-time job in order to become an important contributing member of our team 





Compensation:

*$85,000PHP monthly salary (paid twice per month) + 13th Month

*Paid national Regular Holidays (10 days) and national Special Holidays (8 days)

*Paid Vacation Days (7 days per year)

*Health Insurance Contributions after 60 Days of $3,000PHP

*Annual Anniversary "14th Month" Pay





***Salary and/or additional Bonus Opportunity Considerations - knowledge and effective use of AI & automation tools in order to improve automation and effectiveness within our team will be considered and rewarded***

title: Short-Form Video Editor (TikTok / Reels / Shorts) for NYC Diamond Brand
description:
We're Stienhardt (
), a New York City lab-grown diamond and engagement ring company. We sell direct to consumer and our social channels do real numbers: over 200K on TikTok and over 125K on Instagram. We publish education-first content about diamonds: how they're cut, how to read a lab report, what actually matters when you buy an engagement ring. Serious about diamonds, not stuffy about it.



What you'll do



Edit short-form vertical video (9:16) for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts from raw footage we provide: ring b-roll, macro diamond shots, voiceover scripts, and screen recordings

Cut for retention: strong hook in the first 2 seconds, tight pacing, no dead air

Add clean captions/subtitles on every video (burned-in, styled to our brand fonts, which we'll provide)

Color-correct jewelry footage so diamonds look accurate and bright, not blown out or yellow

Batch-edit: you'll typically get scripts and footage for several videos at once and deliver them as a set

Follow a written brand style guide (we have one, it's specific, and we'll train you on it)

You're a fit if you have



2+ years editing short-form social video, with a portfolio of vertical videos to prove it

CapCut and/or Premiere Pro proficiency

A real feel for TikTok/Reels pacing and trends, not just technical editing skill

Strong written English comprehension (our scripts are precise and the on-screen text must match them exactly)

Reliable internet and a machine that can handle 1080p+ editing without choking

Attention to detail. In jewelry, a typo or a wrong claim in on-screen text is a real problem, so we need someone who checks their work.





Bonus points for



Experience editing for jewelry, luxury, fashion, or beauty brands

Basic motion graphics (After Effects or CapCut equivalents)

Thumbnail/cover-frame design

How we work



Fully async. No meetings-heavy culture, no timezone nightmare. We assign work in batches with clear briefs and deadlines. We'd like 1 to 2 hours of overlap with US Eastern time a few days a week for feedback, but the editing itself happens on your schedule so long as deliverables are received in timely manner.

ta Ads Manager and/or Google Ads showing campaign performance. Client names and sensitive information may be redacted.

title: Sales Consultant – Photography Albums, Wall Art & Prints
description:
**$5 USD per hour to start, plus performance bonuses**



We are a high-end photography studio based in New Jersey, USA, looking for a friendly, confident Sales Consultant to help our clients preserve their memories through albums, wall art, and prints.



This is **not cold calling**. You'll be speaking with clients who have already completed a photography session with us and are excited to see their images.



**This role is ideal for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people make purchasing decisions—not someone who relies on high-pressure sales tactics.**



You'll meet with clients over Zoom or Google Meet, share your screen, present their photographs using Fundy Designer, and help them choose the artwork that is right for their home and family. Our clients invest in premium artwork that will be displayed and enjoyed for years, so your role is to educate, guide, and help them make the best decision for their family.



## What You'll Do



* Call clients after their photography session to schedule ordering appointments.

* Conduct sales appointments over Zoom or Google Meet.

* Share your screen and present photographs using Fundy Designer. Training will be provided.

* Help clients select their favorite photographs.

* Recommend albums, framed prints, canvases, wall art, gift prints, and other artwork.

* Follow up with clients who have not completed their order.

* Keep accurate and detailed notes in our CRM.

* Create an exceptional client experience from beginning to end.



## Requirements



* Excellent spoken and written English. This is extremely important.

* A friendly, warm, and professional personality.

* Strong communication and sales skills.

* Comfortable speaking with clients on video calls.

* Reliable internet connection.

* A quiet and professional workspace.

* Organized, dependable, and comfortable following up with clients.

* Photography, portrait sales, customer service, or retail sales experience is a plus.



## Training



You do not need previous experience with Fundy Designer. We'll teach you:



* How to use Fundy Designer.

* Our sales process.

* How to recommend artwork naturally without being pushy.

* How to handle common client questions and concerns.

* How to create an excellent client experience.



## Hours



The schedule is flexible, but you must be available during some U.S. Eastern Time hours, including occasional evenings when clients are available.



## Pay



* **$5 USD per hour to start**

* Performance bonuses based on sales.

* Opportunities for raises as you grow with the company.



## How to Apply



Please send:



* Your resume.

* A 2–3 minute video introducing yourself in English.

* A brief explanation of your sales or customer service experience.



Please also include the phrase:



**"Beautiful memories deserve beautiful homes."**



This lets us know you read the entire job posting.



## Video Challenge



At the end of your introduction video, act out how you would respond if a client said:



> **"I love these photos, but this is more than I planned to spend."**



Do not explain what you would do. Respond as though you are speaking directly to the client during a real sales appointment. Continue the conversation naturally for at least **60–90 seconds**, as if you were speaking with a real client.



**Please record this portion in one continuous take without stopping or editing.**



**Applications that do not include the video challenge may not be considered.**

title: Direct-Response Video Editor — Short-Form + VSL Ads (UGC / Story / Animation / Native)
description:
We're a story-driven DTC brand hiring a direct-response editor to cut ads for
, Instagram, and TikTok. One brand, long-term, real room to grow with us.



Read this before applying, because it's the whole job:



We are not hiring a videographer. We're hiring an editor who thinks like a marketer. Your work is judged on one thing — did the ad stop the scroll and hold it — not on how cinematic it looks. Clarity beats cleverness. We chase response, not aesthetics. If your instinct with raw footage is to color-grade it, add slick transitions, and "clean it up," we're not a fit — and that's okay.



What you'll actually be cutting

Ads that feel like a real person posted them, not like a brand ran them — UGC-style testimonials, emotional story ads, animation ads, VSLs, AI-voiceover + b-roll ads, text-on-screen ads, native creatives, hooks, product demos. Raw and real beats polished, every time. The goal is to not make it look like an ad.



The craft we expect (this is the standard, not a wishlist)

You understand concepts, not just cuts. You get the idea behind an ad — the angle, the belief it shifts, the emotional arc — and you edit to serve it. You can tell why an ad works, second by second, not just that it "looks clean."

You're not tied to one format — you can build whatever the concept needs. UGC testimonial, story ad, VSL, AI-voiceover-over-b-roll, text-on-screen, split-screen, before/after, static-to-video, animation. You pick the format that serves the idea and you can cut all of them well.

Animation ads. You can build animated story ads and simple 3D/animated explainers that make an invisible mechanism visible — showing the viewer what's happening so the idea lands instantly.

Hook in the first 3 seconds. A pattern interrupt that stops the scroll — never a logo or a polite intro. You understand open loops and curiosity gaps and use them to buy the next second.

Retention over everything. Every second earns the next. You cut to an emotional arc — relatability ? tension ? relief — not to a checklist of clips.

You use contrast to control the eye. Black-and-white with a single accent color, before/after, tension into relief, loud into quiet — visual and emotional contrast to pull attention exactly where it needs to go.

B-roll that matches the voiceover word-for-word, and clean text-on-screen that carries the message with the sound off (feeds autoplay muted). Clips run ~3–5s, natural light, no staged studio look, product revealed late — after the story earns it, never up front.

Sound design as timing, not decoration. Music, zoom, and SFX move with the emotion — the track shifts at each structural beat, the zoom lands on the emphasis line, the punch hits on the reveal.

Keep UGC raw. Slightly awkward, imperfect, conversational — that's the authenticity that converts. Don't polish it out.

Native by default: 9:16 vertical, tight or long depending on the concept, fast clean captions/subtitles, no watermarks or bugs.

Tools & workflow

Editing: Premiere / CapCut / Final Cut — whatever you're fastest and sharpest in. We care about output, not software.

Claude is our brain for everything, and it's a big plus if you already work in it: scripts, natural-speech conversion, creative briefs, ad breakdowns, and second-by-second teardowns all run through Claude. The more fluent you are with it, the faster you'll move.

Plus whatever helps you execute better — AI voiceover (ElevenLabs), AI animation/video generation (Kling, Seedance), and spy research on the Meta Ad Library / AdSpy to study winners and losers. Show us the tools that make you faster and sharper.

You'll live in the research loop: study winners and losers, break them down beat-by-beat, form a hypothesis, iterate fast. You're expected to have opinions on why an ad worked — not just assemble footage.

What we provide

Raw footage, scripts and hooks, creative direction, winning-ad examples, and our internal training so you learn our exact style and keep getting better.



What you keep

Base pay plus a performance bonus on every winning ad you cut. The better your ads convert, the more you make.



How to apply (read carefully — incomplete applications are skipped)

This is the filter, on purpose. Do all three or we move on:



1. Portfolio of real DR ads. 3–5 actual ads you cut — UGC, story, VSL, animation, text-on-screen, whatever you're strongest at — vertical, native, made to sell. No wedding videos, no YouTube intros, no cinematic reels, no motion-graphics showreels. If your best work is polished brand films, we're not your brand.



2. Pick a winning ad you admire (any brand) and tell us, in one paragraph, why it works — second by second. Hook, why it holds, where the emotion turns. We're reading for whether you think in concepts and retention or just "nice edits."



3. Answer this: You get raw phone footage of a customer talking about our product — a little awkward, natural light, not "produced." Do you (a) polish it into a clean cinematic testimonial, or (b) keep it raw and slightly imperfect — and why?



Bonus if you've edited ecommerce ads before, can move between formats (UGC, VSL, animation, text-on-screen), work in Claude, communicate clearly, and turn revisions around fast.

Important: you will NOT be writing most of the content or making website changes yourself. The client has an in-house content writer and web developer who execute. Your job is the strategy, the audits, the briefs, the specs, and the measurement. You work directly with me (agency owner); I own the client relationship. You never contact the client directly.



EXACT SCOPE OF WORK



Phase 1 (first 2 weeks): Measure and Diagnose



1. Build a structured panel of 40-60 buyer prompts across four categories: category/discovery questions, problem questions, competitor comparison questions, and brand validation questions. Sourced from buyer language I provide (sales call notes, CRM context), plus your own research.

2. Run a baseline audit: test the full panel across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Copilot, multiple runs per prompt to account for answer variability. Record brand presence, competitor presence, position, sentiment, and every source the AI cites.

3. Deliver a baseline visibility scorecard: where the client appears, where competitors own the answer, share of voice by category.

4. Source-gap analysis: for every prompt where competitors win, identify which third-party domains the AI engines cited. Deliver a ranked target list of the sources we need to get the client into.

5. Technical AEO audit of the client's recently rebuilt website: AI crawler access (robots.txt against GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, etc.), rendering check (is content visible without JavaScript execution), schema presence, sitemap, llms.txt, and brand/entity consistency across web properties. Deliver as a pass/fail list with implementation-ready fix specs for the client's developer.



Phase 2 (weeks 2-12): Act



6. Content mapping: the client has a 30-part video series with full scripts. Map each script against the prompt panel and produce a prioritized page plan.

7. Page briefs (2-3 per week): for each priority page, deliver a brief the client's content writer can draft from without back-and-forth: target question as H1, answer-first structure (direct answer in the first 40-60 words), required statistics with named sources, quotable expert statement, FAQ block, internal links.

8. Review each drafted page for AEO fitness before publish.

9. Schema specs: implementation-ready markup specs (Organization, FAQPage, Article + Person, VideoObject, SoftwareApplication) the client's developer can implement directly. Verify implementation after publish.

10. YouTube optimization for the existing 30-part series: question-phrased titles, cleaned transcripts, answer-first descriptions linking to matching site pages, series playlist structure.

11. Off-site citation coordination driven by the source-gap list: review platform profiles, directory listings, structuring press releases and contributed articles for citability, and an indexable podcast transcript page.



Ongoing: Prove



12. Re-run the full prompt panel every two weeks (tool or documented manual protocol, your choice, I'll approve the method).

13. Monthly report I present to the client: visibility movement vs baseline by question category, share of voice vs named competitors, citations won, and recommended next actions.



REQUIREMENTS



- Demonstrated AEO/GEO work with at least one before/after example of measurably improving a brand's presence in AI-generated answers (be ready to show proof: screenshots, tracking reports)

- Working knowledge of how LLMs select and cite sources (answer-first content, entity signals, schema, third-party authority)

- Hands-on schema markup experience: you write specs a developer implements without questions

- Solid traditional SEO foundation

- Able to write clear content briefs for a non-specialist writer

- Fluent written English, organized, deadline-reliable, comfortable working async

- NDA required before the client's name is shared



NICE TO HAVE



- B2B SaaS experience, ideally insurance, fintech, or another regulated vertical

- YouTube SEO experience

- Familiarity with AI visibility tracking tools (Otterly, LLMrefs, Peec, or a manual methodology you can show)

- LinkedIn Sales Navigator / outbound automation experience (separate workstream, a plus, not required)



ENGAGEMENT



- Part-time, approximately 10-15 hours/week, heavier in the first 3 weeks

- 90-day initial engagement with strong likelihood of ongoing monthly work

- Start within days of hire; Phase 1 deliverables (prompt panel, baseline scorecard, technical audit, source-gap list) due within the first 10 days



SCREENING QUESTIONS (answer all in your application)



1. Describe one engagement where you measurably improved a brand's visibility in AI answers. Starting point, what you did, what changed. Include proof if you can.

2. Walk me through, step by step, how you'd build a buyer-prompt panel for a niche B2B vertical you've never worked in.

3. How do you track AI citation presence over time? Name your tools or manual method. A sample or redacted report puts you at the top of the list.

4. A client has 30 long-form video scripts on technical industry topics. What do you do with them, in what order, and why?

5. Confirm your availability to start this week and deliver Phase 1 within 10 days.



Applications that don't answer the screening questions will not be considered. Generic applications will not be considered.



NOTE: If project implementation is successful, there is an opportunity to work with additional clients on various projects. Expertise across various digital marketing channels (Media buying, SEO, AEO, Cold
 outbound, LinkedIn outbound, content creation, etc.) is also considered for this reason.
